Full reference

swiftlet.healpix_map_utils.check_healpy_pixel_weights(nside, datapath=None)[source]

Check that the healpy pixel weights file for this nside can be found.

Looks for <datapath>/full_weights/healpix_full_weights_nside_XXXX.fits

Returns the datapath to pass to hp.map2alm.

Parameters:

  • nside (int) – nside of the map

  • datapath (str) – directory to check first for the pixel weights

swiftlet.healpix_map_utils.find_healpy_pixel_weights_dir(datapath=None)[source]

Find the healpy pixel weights directory.

Returns the first directory that contains a full_weights/ folder. Check:

  1. the datapath argument

  2. the HEALPY_PIXEL_WEIGHTS environment variable

  3. <venv>/share/healpy-data

Raises FileNotFoundError if none are found.

Parameters:

datapath (str) – directory to check first for the pixel weights

swiftlet.healpix_map_utils.get_common_maps(filenames)[source]

Returns a list of all dataset names common to all files.

Parameters:

filenames (list) – paths to the .hdf5 files

swiftlet.healpix_map_utils.get_related_ipix(ipix, nside, levels, ordering='ring')[source]

Return the parent or child HEALPix pixel indices.

Returns a tuple of (pixel indices at the new resolution, nside of the new map).

Parameters:

  • ipix (int or np.ndarray) – pixel indices in the input map

  • nside (int) – nside of the input map

  • levels (int) – change in HEALPix resolution. Each level increases or decreases nside by a factor of 2. levels > 0 returns child pixels at higher resolution levels < 0 returns parent pixels at lower resolution levels == 0 returns the input pixels unchanged

  • ordering (str) – HEALPix pixel ordering, either ‘ring’ or ‘nested’

swiftlet.healpix_map_utils.healpy_pixel_weights_available(nside=None, datapath=None)[source]

Returns True if healpy pixel weights can be found, otherwise False.

Parameters:

  • nside (int) – nside of the map. If None, check for any pixel weights

  • datapath (str) – directory to check first for the pixel weights

swiftlet.healpix_map_utils.read_rotation_angles(filename)[source]

Read ‘theta’ (co-latitude) and ‘phi’ (longitude) angles from hdf5 file.

Assume that theta and phi are given in radians.

Returns a tuple of (co-latitude, longitude) in degrees.

Parameters:

filename (str) – path to the .hdf5 file containing the rotation angles

swiftlet.healpix_map_utils.rotate_map(base_map, theta, phi, ell_max=None, map_rotator_object=None)[source]

Rotate given map using alm space via the co-latitude and longitude passed as theta and phi.

Returns a tuple, (rotated map, rotator object)

Parameters:

  • base_map (np.ndarray) – healpix map to rotate

  • theta (unyt.unyt_quantity (units of deg or equivalent)) – co-latitude rotation angle

  • phi (unyt.unyt_quantity (units of deg or equivalent)) – longitude rotation angle

  • ell_max (int) – maximum multipole used in the rotation

  • map_rotator_object (healpy.Rotator) – rotator to use. If None, one is created from theta and phi

swiftlet.healpix_map_utils.rotate_map_fast(base_map, theta, phi, nside, ell_max=None, map_rotator_object=None)[source]

Rotate a given map using alm space via the passed as theta (co-latitude) and phi (longitude).

Use the healpy pixel weights for the map to alm transform.

Returns a tuple (rotated map, rotator object)

Parameters:

  • base_map (np.ndarray) – healpix map to rotate

  • theta (unyt.unyt_quantity (units of deg or equivalent)) – co-latitude rotation angle

  • phi (unyt.unyt_quantity (units of deg or equivalent)) – longitude rotation angle

  • nside (int) – nside of the rotated map

  • ell_max (int) – maximum multipole used in the rotation

  • map_rotator_object (healpy.Rotator) – rotator to use. If None, one is created from theta and phi

swiftlet.healpix_map_utils.sum_maps(file_numbers, infile_format, outfile, map_names, required_groups=('InternalCodeUnits', 'Units', 'Shell', '__xrayInfo'))[source]

Write a new .hdf5 file with the datasets being the sum total of the input files datasets.

Parameters:

  • file_numbers (list) – index number of the input files to sum

  • infile_format (str) – formatted path to the input files of a given file number: path/input/file_{file_nr}.hdf5

  • outfile (str) – path and name of the file that will be written

  • map_names (list) – map names to sum together. If [‘common’] use all maps that are found in every input file

  • required_groups (tuple) – required groups with essential attributes for lightcone_io maps

swiftlet.healpix_map_utils.write_rotated_lightcone_chunks(basedir, basename, map_names, theta_arr_deg, phi_arr_deg, output_filename, output_nside, input_nside, remote_dir=None, shell_range=None, unit_conversion_func=None, rotate_nside=None, ell_max=None, save_chunks=False, hdf5_dset_kwargs=<object object>)[source]

For a given set of rotation angles per shell, sum all shells along the line of sight that share the same angles.

Each chunk is rotated and the sum of all chunks is written to the output file.

Parameters:

  • basedir (str) – directory containing the lightcone healpix maps

  • basename (str) – base name of the lightcone healpix map files

  • map_names (list) – map names (quantities or datasets) to sum and rotate in chunks, e.g. [“TotalMass”]

  • theta_arr_deg (np.ndarray or unyt.unyt_array) – theta (co-latitude) values per shell [deg]

  • phi_arr_deg (np.ndarray or unyt.unyt_array) – phi (longitude) values per shell [deg]

  • output_filename (str) – path of the .hdf5 file to write

  • output_nside (int) – nside of the output maps

  • input_nside (int) – nside of the input maps

  • remote_dir (str) – for reading healpix maps from a remote directory as done with lightcone_io

  • shell_range (tuple) – shell number of the minimum and maximum shell to consider. If None, use all shells

  • unit_conversion_func (function) – optional function for additional unit conversion prior to rotating maps

  • rotate_nside (int) – nside the maps are rotated at. If None, use input_nside

  • ell_max (int) – maximum multipole used in the rotation

  • save_chunks (boolean) – If True, write each individual chunk to the output file

  • hdf5_dset_kwargs (dict) – keyword arguments passed to h5py create_dataset. If not given, use gzip compression level 9 with shuffle. If None, default h5py compression applied
